name: Imatinib
how: Blocks the BCR-ABL1 fusion kinase, the broken 'stuck gas pedal' that drives chronic myeloid leukemia.
caveat: Approximated as BCR knockdown. In K562 the BCR-ABL1 fusion is switched on from the BCR promoter, so CRISPRi at BCR also silences the fusion. In RPE1 there is no fusion, so this only lowers normal BCR; imatinib's real effects on normal ABL1, KIT and PDGFR are not modeled.

name: Sotorasib
how: Locks the mutant KRAS G12C protein in its 'off' state by binding a pocket found in 2013.
caveat: Approximated as KRAS knockdown. Sotorasib only binds the G12C mutant form; neither K562 nor RPE1 carries KRAS G12C, so the real drug would do little in these cells.

name: Trametinib
how: Blocks MEK1 and MEK2, relay proteins in the growth-signal chain.
caveat: Approximated as knocking down both MEK genes. A drug blocks protein activity in minutes; a knockdown removes the mRNA over days.

name: Palbociclib
how: Blocks CDK4 and CDK6, enzymes that push a cell past a key checkpoint into division.
caveat: Approximated as knocking down CDK4 and CDK6.

name: Everolimus
how: Partly blocks mTOR, a master switch for cell growth and protein making.
caveat: Approximated as MTOR knockdown, which is stronger than the partial block everolimus gives.

name: Nutlin-3a
how: Pulls MDM2 off p53, freeing the cell's 'guardian' to stop division.
caveat: Approximated as MDM2 knockdown. K562 has broken p53, so nutlin should do little there. RPE1 has working p53, but RPE1 MDM2 was not measured: the prediction comes from K562 and very likely misses the p53 response.

name: Olaparib
how: Blocks PARP1, a DNA-repair enzyme; cells that already lack BRCA repair can't cope.
caveat: Approximated as PARP1 knockdown. Olaparib also traps PARP1 on DNA, which knockdown does not mimic.

name: Navitoclax
how: Blocks BCL-XL (and BCL-2), 'anti-death' proteins cancer cells lean on to survive.
caveat: Approximated as BCL2L1 knockdown only; BCL2 was not measured in this dataset.

name: Methotrexate
how: Blocks DHFR, starving dividing cells of the building blocks for new DNA.
caveat: Approximated as DHFR knockdown.

name: 5-Fluorouracil
how: Blocks thymidylate synthase, which makes one of DNA's four letters.
caveat: Approximated as TYMS knockdown. 5-FU also gets built into RNA, which is not modeled.

name: Hydroxyurea
how: Blocks ribonucleotide reductase, the enzyme that turns RNA letters into DNA letters.
caveat: Approximated as RRM2 knockdown.

name: Gemcitabine
how: A fake DNA letter that jams DNA copying and blocks ribonucleotide reductase.
caveat: Approximated as RRM1 knockdown. Gemcitabine's main effect, getting built into DNA, is not modeled.

name: Etoposide
how: Traps topoisomerase II while it has cut DNA, leaving broken DNA behind.
caveat: Approximated as TOP2A knockdown, which is a poor stand-in: the drug's DNA breaks are not mimicked by removing the enzyme. Treat this one with extra suspicion.

name: Topotecan
how: Traps topoisomerase I on DNA, causing DNA damage when the cell copies its genome.
caveat: Approximated as TOP1 knockdown, a poor stand-in for a DNA-damaging 'poison'. The 3D structure shows camptothecin, the natural compound topotecan was derived from.

name: Bortezomib
how: Jams the proteasome, the cell's protein shredder, so damaged proteins pile up.
caveat: Approximated as PSMB5 knockdown.

name: Selinexor
how: Blocks XPO1, the 'exit door' that ships proteins out of the nucleus.
caveat: Approximated as XPO1 knockdown.

name: Volasertib
how: Blocks PLK1, a kinase needed to split chromosomes during division.
caveat: Approximated as PLK1 knockdown.

name: Alisertib
how: Blocks Aurora A, a kinase that builds the spindle used in division.
caveat: Approximated as AURKA knockdown.

name: Ceralasertib
how: Blocks ATR, an alarm protein that pauses the cell when DNA copying goes wrong.
caveat: Approximated as ATR knockdown.

name: Adavosertib
how: Blocks WEE1, a brake that stops cells entering division with damaged DNA.
caveat: Approximated as WEE1 knockdown.

name: Brequinar
how: Blocks DHODH, an enzyme on the mitochondria that makes DNA and RNA letters.
caveat: Approximated as DHODH knockdown.

name: JQ1
how: Knocks BRD4 off DNA, turning down growth genes like MYC.
caveat: Approximated as BRD4 knockdown.
